title: Artifact Registry Push/Pull and Vulnerability Scan

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `google:gcp:pubsub:message` events with `protoPayload.serviceName="artifactregistry.googleapis.com"` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.3.16 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `google:gcp:pubsub:message` traffic without `protoPayload.serviceName="artifactregistry.googleapis.com"`. Confirm UC-4.3.16 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

description: UC-4.3.16 — Artifact Registry Push/Pull and Vulnerability Scan: queries Google Cloud `google:gcp:pubsub:message` for search criteria `protoPayload.serviceName="artifactregistry.googleapis.com"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, detecting 'Artifact Registry Push/Pull and Vulnerability Scan' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.3.16 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Forward Artifact Registry audit logs via Pub/Sub. Ingest Container Analysis for CVE findings. Alert on critical/high in production repos. Baseline push/pull by principal; alert on anomalies.
visualization: Table (repo, method, count), Bar chart (top push/pull), Table (image, CVE, severity).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Forward Artifact Registry audit logs via Pub/Sub. Ingest Container Analysis for CVE findings. Alert on critical/high in production repos. Baseline push/pull by principal; alert on anomalies.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" protoPayload.serviceName="artifactregistry.googleapis.com"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.16_artifact_registry_push_p_16"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect artifact registry push/pull and vulnerability scan. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_16_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (repo, method, count), Bar chart (top push/pull), Table (image, CVE, severity)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of artifact registry push/pull and vulnerability scan so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
